title: Go SDK: composable streaming API with context-aware cancellation and deadline semantics
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Current Go SDK streaming surface is fragile in real-world servers and client code: callers frequently leak goroutines when contexts are cancelled, timeouts are ambiguous (per-request vs overall stream deadline), and retries interact poorly with partially-consumed streams. Scope: Implement a composable streaming API for the Go SDK that provides explicit context propagation, clear deadline vs timeout semantics, ergonomic helpers for common patterns (client usage in HTTP handlers, background workers), and example snippets. Goals: 1) Ensure no goroutine leaks when callers cancel or timeout. 2) Provide primitives for resumable/idempotent retry strategies for streaming endpoints. 3) Offer small, well-documented examples demonstrating correct usage in HTTP handlers and background tasks. Acceptance criteria: - New API surface merged with unit and integration tests covering cancellation, deadline expiry, server EOF, and retry backoff interactions. - Benchmarks showing <2% added latency for non-cancel paths. - Example snippets added to docs repo and included in SDK quickstart. - API approved by SDK and infra owners and released under sdk-go-1.4.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelable StreamReader that returns immediately on context cancellation with explicit Close() semantics
Clear docs and examples for per-request timeouts vs total stream deadlines
Retryable stream wrapper that can replay from known safe offsets or uses idempotency token pattern
Unit tests for context cancellation, deadline expiry, server-initiated EOF, and partial message handling
Integration test using local test harness simulating slow servers and abrupt connection closes
API review sign-off from eng-sdks and infra teams
design_notes: We will add a StreamClient interface: Subscribe(ctx, params) (Stream, error) where Stream exposes Next(ctx) (Message, error) and Close() error. Next should respect the ctx passed in and always return quickly on ctx.Done(). Messages are simple bytes + metadata; SDK will provide a Reader adapter to allow io.Copy-like consumption without leaking goroutines. For retries: streaming endpoints will expose a resumable cursor field in Message.Metadata.Cursor; the RetryableStream wrapper will use that when replaying. For non-resumable streams, we recommend idempotency tokens on the original request and fall back to non-retryable behavior. Timeout semantics: callers can choose per-call ctx with > or < parent ctx deadline; examples will show when to use child contexts with timeouts. We'll add two small helpers: WithStreamTimeout(ctx, d) and StreamToChannel(ctx, stream) which preserve cancellation semantics and ensure Close is called in all code paths.
implementation_plan: 1) Add StreamClient and Stream types to sdk-go v0.1 package with minimal methods
2) Implement ctx-aware Next(ctx) and Close() with tests ensuring immediate wake-up on ctx cancel
3) Implement Reader adapter and unit tests to verify no goroutine leaks (use leaktest helper)
4) Implement RetryableStream wrapper with cursor-based replay support and exponential backoff + jitter
5) Write integration tests in infra/test-harness that simulate server pauses and resets
6) Add docs and three example programs: http-handler pattern, background worker, resumable-download pattern
7) API review, address feedback, bump release to sdk-go-1.4 and release notes
notes: Trade-offs considered: - Returning a fully buffered message vs streaming raw chunks: we choose chunked Message for memory-sensitive workloads but provide Reader adapter for user convenience. - Automatic retries for non-resumable streams are dangerous; prefer explicit idempotency or resume cursors. - API ergonomics prioritize minimal surface area for common cases; advanced users can pull lower-level primitives.
